question: Using Figure 6B-1 and Section 6B.06, list the main TTC-zone areas in travel order and identify the three components of the activity area.
model_answer: Direct Answer: In the order encountered by traffic, a TTC zone is typically divided into four areas: the advance warning area, the transition area, the activity area, and the termination area. The activity area — the section of highway where the work actually takes place — is itself comprised of three components: the work space, the traffic space, and the buffer space. This information is explanatory (Support) rather than a mandatory requirement. Visual evidence: [Image 1] (Figure 6B-1) shows the four areas in travel order from bottom (upstream) to top (downstream) — the advance warning area ("tells traffic what to expect ahead"), the transition area ("moves traffic out of its normal path" via a taper of channelizing devices), the activity area ("is where work takes place") containing the hatched work space, the traffic space allowing traffic to pass through, and both lateral and longitudinal buffer spaces, and finally the termination area ("lets traffic resume normal operations") with a downstream taper. Citations: - Section 6B.03 Support §1 (p.771) - Section 6B.06 Support §1 (p.773) - Section 6B.06 Support §5 (p.773) - Figure 6B-1 (p.772)
gold_answer: Advance warning, transition, activity, and termination. The activity area consists of the work space, traffic space, and buffer space.
